newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to raise state pension fund limit on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to raise state pension fund limit on stocks.

text.p: Taiwan's top state examination body, The Examination Yuan, has decided to raise the limit of the state employee pension fund's local stock holdings to 30 percent from the current 10 percent, local newspapers said on Sunday.
The Commercial Times said the state employee pension fund would be allowed to commission local or foreign fund management companies to manage up to 20 percent of its holdings in stocks.
The fund, worth an estimated T$24 billion, can currently invest up to 10 percent of its holdings in stocks and such holdings would still be managed by the fund itself, the newspaper said.

The new 30 percent limit would mean that some T$7.2 billion would be allowed to be invested in stocks, the newspaper said, adding that the fund is expected to start entering the stock market in early 1997.

The Examination Yuan, which oversees the fund management, has negotiated with related government offices such as the Finance Ministry and the central bank about the proposal, the Commercial Times said. The Examination Yuan is expected to formally announce its decision soon, the newpaper added.
The move followed a cabinet panel's approval on Friday to allow the T$188 billion state labour insurance fund to invest up to 30 percent of its holdings, or T$56.4 billion, in the local stock market.
The insurance fund is expected to start trading in stocks in mid-November.
The cabinet's decision helped lifted the stock index on Saturday to close up 107.83 points, or 1.67 percent, at 6,562.94.
The Economic Daily News said a total of T$100 billion worth of government funds would be available for stock investments in early 1997.
